items.stem: Several microservices call each other synchronously, so one service's slowness stalls the whole request chain. Which pattern most directly contains this failure?

options.text: A circuit breaker with timeouts on the dependency call
options.rationale: Correct: a circuit breaker plus timeouts stops calls to a failing dependency from blocking the caller.

options.text: Sharing a single database across all services
options.rationale: A shared database increases coupling and does not contain call-chain failures.
Removing async messaging increases synchronous coupling, worsening the problem.

options.text: Deploying all services as one unit
options.rationale: That recreates a monolith rather than containing the failure.

items.explanation: Correct: a circuit breaker plus timeouts stops calls to a failing dependency from blocking the caller.

items.stem: A business operation spans three services and must stay consistent without a distributed transaction. Which pattern fits?

options.rationale: Correct: a saga coordinates local transactions and compensates on failure, giving eventual consistency without 2PC.

options.text: A two-phase commit across all three databases
options.rationale: Distributed 2PC is the pattern microservices avoid due to coupling and availability costs.

options.text: A single shared transaction table locked by all services
options.rationale: A shared lock reintroduces tight coupling and a bottleneck.
The requirement is to stay consistent, so ignoring it is not a valid option.

items.explanation: Correct: a saga coordinates local transactions and compensates on failure, giving eventual consistency without 2PC.

items.stem: Which TWO guidelines lead to healthy microservice boundaries? (Select TWO)

options.text: Align each service to a business capability or bounded context
options.rationale: Correct: capability-aligned services change for one reason and stay cohesive.

options.text: Give each service ownership of its own data
options.rationale: Correct: private data ownership reduces coupling and lets services evolve independently.

options.text: Split services by technical layer (UI, logic, data)
options.rationale: Layer-based splits spread one change across many services.

options.text: Share one database schema across all services
options.rationale: A shared schema couples services and blocks independent change.

items.explanation: Correct: capability-aligned services change for one reason and stay cohesive.
